# Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#37
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:M, area:tools, epic:extension-points

Part of #35

## Why

`ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model. The shipped example shows the
shape of the problem: `example/weather-tool.ts` declares `location` as a required string, then
casts and defaults it (`(input.location as string) || 'Unknown'`) with a comment warning the reader
that `inputSchema` shapes what the model sends but does not enforce it. That is the careful version,
written by the people who wrote the engine — and it still answers a malformed call with a
confidently formatted forecast for `'Unknown'` rather than telling the model it got the call wrong.

The registry currently pushes this check onto each tool's own executor, leaving every consumer
to implement it itself — differently each time, or not at all. A tool that receives unexpected input must fail
in one predictable, known way before the rest of this epic's tool work can be built on top
of it.

## What to do

Validate `input` against the resolved tool definition's `inputSchema` inside
`ToolRegistry.execute`, before the executor runs, using a JSON Schema validator (`ajv`
unless the build proves otherwise) added to `dependencies` — not a second, hand-written
schema in a different format, since the schema already has to match what is handed to the
providers.

Compile a static tool's schema once at `register` time so a broken schema fails at startup,
not mid-conversation; a schema produced by a function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource`
resolves and compiles per call, cached by the resolved schema object.

A rejection returns a `ToolResponse` (`{result: '<what was wrong>'}`) rather than throwing,
so a malformed call becomes something the model can read and correct within the existing
`DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5` budget, instead of ending the whole conversation with a
generic transport error. Validation enforces `required`, declared types and `enum` only —
it does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults, and
there is no opt-out flag.

Update `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against the resolved definition's
      `inputSchema` before calling the executor; on failure it returns a `ToolResponse`
      whose `result` describes the failure, and the executor is never invoked
- [ ] A new `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` (the registry has no test file today)
      registers a tool requiring a `location` string, calls `execute` with `{}`, and
      asserts the returned result names `location` as required and the executor's call
      count is `0`
- [ ] A test asserts valid input with an unlisted extra property is passed through to the
      executor unchanged (`toEqual`, so an added default or coerced value fails the test) —
      exactly once
- [ ] A test asserts a wrong-typed field (a number where a string is required) is rejected
      with a message naming the field path and the expected type, and that the message does
      **not** contain the offending value
- [ ] A test asserts `register` throws at registration time for an uncompilable schema, and
      that the thrown message names the tool
- [ ] A test asserts a function-valued tool definition whose returned schema differs between
      calls is validated against the schema current at that call, not a stale cached one
- [ ] A test asserts a static tool's schema is compiled once across ten `execute` calls
- [ ] A tool-loop test in `chatOrchestrator.test.ts` drives a stub provider through a
      rejected tool call followed by a corrected retry, and asserts `processMessage`
      resolves — not rejects — with the rejection text visible to the provider on the next
      round
- [ ] `execute` still throws `Unknown tool: <name>` for an unregistered name, unchanged,
      pinned by a test
- [ ] Rejection messages and log lines name the failing property paths and the constraint
      that failed, and never a property **value**. Tool input is where identifying data
      enters the engine and the engine redacts nothing today. A test asserts a rejected
      payload containing an identifying field produces no log line and no returned text
      containing that field's value
- [ ] `execute` carries a **one-line** doc comment — `re-lint/max-comment-lines` rejects a
      `@param`/`@returns`/`@throws` block — and the full contract (rejection `ToolResponse` for input

- [ ] `docs/adding-a-tool.md` no longer tells executors to cast defensively and handle

## Tech notes

Today's `throw` in `registry.ts` propagates through the orchestrator's tool-call
`Promise.all`, out of the processing loop's `try`, fires `onError`, and reaches the
WebSocket error handler, which sends a generic "Failed to process message" and never sends
the stream-end frame. That end-to-end path is why a rejection has to be a returned
`ToolResponse` instead of a throw.

Deliberately out of scope: the `Unknown tool: <name>` throw stays as-is — the same failure
class handled the opposite way, which is an intentional split, but changing it affects
direct callers and is tracked as *Return an unknown tool name to the model instead of
throwing*. Also out of scope: validating tool *output*; hallucination detection and an
evaluation harness; per-tool authorization — a schema-valid call for someone else's data is still
valid, and authorization is a separate `ToolContext` boundary concern that no issue in this epic
owns (*Let a consumer decline a tool call through a `beforeToolCall` hook* is a veto seam, not an
authorization model); retry, timeout
and rate limiting around tool execution; and any actual tool implementation, which is
written against this contract later.

# Definition of Done

> `ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
> without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
> Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
> providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model.

**Strategy: `direct`** — `ToolRegistry.register`, `ToolRegistry.execute` and `createChatOrchestrator` already expose the exact entry points this ticket changes, so the acceptance tests call them directly today and fail because schema compilation and input validation are absent.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor** — `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against `inputSchema`, returns a `ToolResponse` naming the missing required property, and does not invoke the executor.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [ ] **rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs** — `ToolRegistry.execute` rejects a property with the wrong JSON Schema type without calling the executor, names the failing field path and expected type in `result`, and omits the offending property value from both `result` and emitted log lines.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [ ] **throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled** — `ToolRegistry.register` compiles a static `ToolDefinition`'s `inputSchema` once at registration time and throws synchronously naming the tool when the schema is invalid.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [ ] **returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round** — `createChatOrchestrator` feeds a schema-rejected tool call's `ToolResponse.result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` without invoking the executor on the invalid call, allowing the model to retry with valid arguments and complete the turn.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

specs/hal-engine-providers/spec.md:101:Supports streaming through `sendMessage` and structured JSON output through `generateStructured` ([validated by: streams text chunks from Vertex AI response](../../src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts#L55), [structured](../../src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts#L208)).
specs/hal-engine-providers/spec.md:157:- A function call part becomes a `tool_use` chunk. Vertex reports no call id of its own, so the function's name is used as the id as well ([validated by: yields tool_use chunks for function calls](../../src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts#L76)).
specs/hal-engine-providers/spec.md:158:- A `MAX_TOKENS` finish reason becomes the stop reason `max_tokens`, so a truncated reply is distinguishable from a completed one ([validated by: maps MAX_TOKENS finish reason](../../src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts#L110)).
specs/hal-engine-providers/spec.md:159:- A candidate carrying no parts is skipped rather than emitted as an empty chunk ([validated by: skips chunks with no candidate parts](../../src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts#L158)).
specs/hal-engine-providers/spec.md:160:- The `assistant` role is sent to Vertex as `model`, which is the only role name its API accepts for a prior reply; `user` passes through unchanged ([validated by: maps assistant role to model for Vertex API](../../src/providers/vertex/vertexProvider.test.ts#L175)).

specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md:512:A model often narrates before it calls a tool. That narration is streamed to the client as it arrives, so by the time the tool asks for suppression the client is already displaying it. It cannot be skipped; it is retracted.
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:324:6. If the tool set `suppressAssistantResponse`, the AI's next reply is kept in session context but hidden from the frontend ([validated by: asks for suppression when the tool says the reply is already handled](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L466))
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:325:7. The orchestrator re-queries the AI provider with the updated messages, and the chunks of every round reach the client in order ([validated by: runs another round after a tool call and streams both rounds in order](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L401))
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:326:8. This repeats while `round <= maxToolRounds`, counted from zero, so the default of 5 permits six model calls in total ([validated by: stops asking for tools once maxToolRounds is spent](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L422))
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:337:- The loop ends as soon as a round stops with `end_turn`, and nothing further is asked of the provider ([validated by: stops after one round when nothing asked for a tool](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L413)).
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:339:- The response text a hook sees is the text of every round joined, not only the last ([validated by: joins the text of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L478)).
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:340:- Usage an earlier round reported is kept when a later round reports none, so a tool round does not erase the token count ([validated by: keeps the usage an earlier round reported when a later round reports none](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L500)).

## Validation at execute time

- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16); [validated by: rejects input missing a required property without calling the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L9)).
- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46); [validated by: rejects a wrong-typed nested property with a redacted path-aware message](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L37)).
- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults ([validated by: passes valid input with extra properties through unchanged exactly once](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L76)).
- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.
  ([validated by: throws the unchanged unknown-tool error](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L189))

## Schema compilation and caching

- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94)).
- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: compiles a static schema once across repeated executions](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L166)).
- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: compiles a function-source schema once when the same schema object is reused](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L103); [validated by: validates function-source input against the schema returned for each call](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L134)).

## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery
    G --> H{round <= maxToolRounds?}
    H -->|yes| A
    H -->|no| D
```

Here is what the message handler does when a tool call comes through:

1. The model yields a `tool_use` chunk with tool name and input
2. The handler creates a `ToolEntry` and sends it to the client via `entry_upsert`
3. The orchestrator executes the tool (via `ToolRegistry.execute()`)
4. Tool results get added to the conversation as a `tool_result` message
5. If the tool returned `clientMessages`, they are forwarded to the frontend as-is, in one `tool_result` chunk ([validated by: forwards the client messages a tool returned as one tool_result chunk](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L436))
6. If the tool set `suppressAssistantResponse`, the AI's next reply is kept in session context but hidden from the frontend ([validated by: asks for suppression when the tool says the reply is already handled](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L503))
7. The orchestrator re-queries the AI provider with the updated messages, and the chunks of every round reach the client in order ([validated by: runs another round after a tool call and streams both rounds in order](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L438))
8. This repeats while `round <= maxToolRounds`, counted from zero, so the default of 5 permits six model calls in total ([validated by: stops asking for tools once maxToolRounds is spent](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L459))

### Whether a round continues

- A round continues only when the model stopped for `tool_use`, named at least one tool, and a `ToolRegistry` is configured ([validated by: continues when the model requested a tool and a registry can run it](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L11)).
- With no registry configured the loop stops, whatever the model asked for, because nothing could execute the call ([validated by: stops when no registry is configured, whatever the model asked for](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L15)).
- A `tool_use` stop naming no tool stops the loop, rather than re-querying with nothing to add ([validated by: stops when the model named no tool](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L19)).
- Any other stop reason ends the loop even when tool calls are pending ([validated by: stops when the model finished for a reason other than tool use](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L23)).

### Across rounds

- The loop ends as soon as a round stops with `end_turn`, and nothing further is asked of the provider ([validated by: stops after one round when nothing asked for a tool](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L450)).
- An `entry_upsert` a tool returns is appended to the session and its index rewritten to the position it actually landed in, because a tool cannot know how long the session already is ([validated by: appends an upserted entry to the session and rewrites its index to match](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L449)).
- The response text a hook sees is the text of every round joined, not only the last ([validated by: joins the text of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L515)).
- Usage an earlier round reported is kept when a later round reports none, so a tool round does not erase the token count ([validated by: keeps the usage an earlier round reported when a later round reports none](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L537)).

The frontend shows a spinner on the last tool entry while the stream is still processing (`isProcessing` is `true`). The `stream_end` message clears the processing state, which hides the spinner. This works correctly even when tool suppression prevents assistant entries from reaching the frontend. See [tool-responses.md](../hal-engine-tool-responses/spec.md) for details on client messages and suppression.
